Results.ReviewText: For years, I used a propane gas grill. Then I went several years without a grill. Recently, my wife purchased for us a weber 22 inch grill. I was skeptical about the hassle of using charcoal, the quality of the heat, etc. Boy, was I clueless. The instructions that came with the Weber Grill were very easy to follow, using the lighter cubes in the charcoal containers is very easy. But, that’s not the best part. The best part is without question the ridiculously good taste of steaks and chicken that I cooked on the grill. It is so easy to fire up the charcoal, preheat the grill, put the meat on the grill, close the hood, wait 7-8 minutes, open the hood flip it over and close the hood, wait 7-8 minutes and then have high-quality restaurant tender meats. Count me in as somebody who will never go back to propane.

Results.ReviewText:
I had a 22" grill for over 20 years. The lower air vent blades had burned and rusted to the point where they no longer could control the air flow, were rusted beyond replaceability, and I finally decided to replace it with the current model of what I've been using, the Premium. After assembling it and finding some annoyances, most significant, the loss of the "bail" lid holder, I returned it and exchanged it for the Master Touch. I've been using it for a month now and I'm reluctantly trying to accept it because it's as good as I'm going to get. Still, I find several things that are, for no reason I can see, have been changed from my older model, and make it more inconvenient to use. They may seem small and insignificant, but they're annoying.

1. Things have been turned around. The lower air vent handle used to be on the left and is now on the right where I always seem to have something in the way when I want to adjust it.

2. The handle on the lid has been turned 90 degrees relative to the upper vent and thermometer so now I have to stand to the side of the grill rather than in front in order to raise the lid and "park" it in the bail. 

3. The "hole in the grill" is just plain dumb! I've wired it in place so it doesn't fall out when I remove the grill to load in the charcoal. I'll probably weld it. It would make more sense to offer the removable center as an option and make a full surface grill standard. 

I could go on and on, but really, I liked the old one better and I'm really having difficulty adjusting to the new one. But what's a Weber fan to do?

Results.ReviewText:
I purchased this 22" master touch kettle from home depot back in May 2019. I have a WSM 14.5" charcoal smoker and love it, but I typically grill with my Weber Genesis gas grill so this was my first time using a charcoal kettle. The one touch cleaning system and the ash catcher are great (I've used the basic kettle that only has an ash catch pan and it's a pain/less safe, especially when it's windy). I love that this version has the lid holder (the premium version only has a hook on the inside. I wouldn't mind having the hook also on the lid so you can use both holders. Sometimes I feel the hook would work well when starting your chimney and the current lid holder is great when flipping your food. 

The accessories work well overall. Once my chimney is ready and I pour the coals into the charcoal baskets, I set my chimney on the shelf on the bottom of the kettle on it's side until it cools. The charcoal baskets allow you to easily push them together for direct heat v. put them on the sides, using the sides as direct zones and the center as an indirect zone (this is primarily how I cook, I sear on direct heat and cook the meat through on indirect heat if needed). The main grate has the flip up sides which are great for adding coals during a longer cook or adding wood chips/chunks. The grate also has the center removable section for the custom cooking accessories. This is nice for flexibility, but I'd like to see clips or something to keep this attached to the base grate when you aren't using the center cooking accessories. I like to hang my grate on the kettle when using my chimney and the center grate being loose is a pain. The additional raised/elevate grate works well for burger buns, etc. 

Overall this is hard to beat for $200-$220. I'm used to paying $600 or more for a weber gas grill and love the cheaper charcoal option for cookouts on nicer days. If you have a deck or patio, buy a separate grilling mat to catch drippings. Otherwise this is a great kettle.

Results.ReviewText: It is good and comes with all the goodies — but the outside enamel quality is not the same as you can see ripples and waves .
Results.Title: It is good —but...

Results.ReviewText: I like the sides that flip up to add wood chips or charcoal.
Results.Title: Great grill.

Results.ReviewText: Master touch is definitely the way to go if you’re going with the stand alone kettle,the extra features are well worth it. I really like a couple of the subtle changes ,the ash catcher seems easier to remove on the new colored kettles and I like the holes in the ring that holds the ash catcher to know where the vents are set. the charcoal baskets,lid holder and the extra height are my favorite features on the master touch. If you’re on the fence about getting one don’t be these are made to last and are very versatile you can grill and smoke low and slow in these things
Results.Title: Great grill

Results.ReviewText: I purchased this solely for the ivory color. It looks better in person. Added the Weber wooden side table, it looks so retro with that added feature!!
Results.Title: Awesome color!

Results.ReviewText: I'm no stranger to the Weber game but I've been waiting for years to get ahold of an Ivory kettle.  I'm so glad Weber decided to release the additional colors here in the U.S.
Results.Title: Beautiful finish on this kettle.  It POPS!

14501001.Name: 22” Master-Touch™ Charcoal Grill
14501001.Description: Some things never go out of style—like the smoky flavor of charcoal, the sizzle of a summer cookout, and the iconic silhouette of the 22" Master-Touch™ Charcoal Grill. This grill features a handy Tuck-Away Lid Holder that gives you a convenient place to nest the lid against the side of the bowl, a hinged cooking grate that fits circular GBS accessories so you can explore more ways to cook, a built-in lid thermometer, and legs that are 2” taller than standard kettles. Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retain heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results. When it’s time to clean up, the One-Touch™ cleaning system makes it neat and effortless—just swipe the lever to clear ashes into the enclosed, high-capacity ash catcher. Two wheels make it easy to roll this timeless classic to the center of the action, right where it belongs. Because some grills don’t just cook food, they make memories.· Porcelain-enameled finish is scratch and rust-resistant· Room to cook for 6-8 people· Hinged, plated-steel cooking grate fits circular GBS grillware· Included Char-Rails make it easy to arrange charcoal· Lid thermometer makes it easy to see grill temperature· Adjustable lid and bowl dampers let you control temperature· Tuck-Away Lid Holder provides handy space to hang lid· 2 tool hooks included on bowl handle· One-Touch™ cleaning system sweeps ash into enclosed catcher· Easy to move on two durable, all-weather wheels.· Heat-resistant lid and bowl handles· Bottom, wire storage shelf· Durable fuel grate· 3 aluminum legs are rust-resistant and 2” taller· 10-year limited warranty
